Kenneth Loyd'''{{cite web |title=Jordan Loyd |url=https://www.acb.com/jugador/temporada-a-temporada/id/30000046 |website=ACB.COM |access-date=May 14, 2025}} (born July 27, 1993) is an American–born naturalised Polish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]], and [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland national team]]. He won an [[2019 NBA Finals|NBA championship]] in 2019 with the [[2018–19 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman Paladins]] and [[Indianapolis Greyhounds men's basketball|Indianapolis Greyhounds]]. ==Early life and college career== Loyd attended [[Milton High School (Georgia)|Milton High School]] in [[Milton, Georgia]], where he led Milton to a playoff appearance in each of his final two seasons, including a state championship as a junior in 2009–10.{{cite news|title=J Milton basketball team wins first state title |url=https://www.appenmedia.com/sports/milton-basketball-team-wins-first-state-title/article_54ed3666-20ec-5229-bca0-3a8eb9a8c786.html|access-date=April 28, 2023|author=Hatcher Hurd|work=appenmedia.com|date=Mar 18, 2010}} Loyd earned all-conference and team MVP honors as a senior after leading his squad to a top-five national ranking.{{cite news|title=Jordan Loyd - UIndy Athletics|url=https://athletics.uindy.edu/roster.aspx?rp_id=4939|access-date=October 30, 2018|work=UIndy.edu}} In 2011–12 in his freshman year at [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman University]], he averaged 6 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. In 2012-13 he redshirted. In 2013–14 in his sophomore year, Loyd transferred from Furman to the [[Indianapolis Greyhounds|University of Indianapolis]], where he quickly became a key part of the UIndy bench, averaging double-digits minutes. On 2014–15 in his junior year he averaged 15.6 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game with a .484 field goal percentage, and a .420 percentage from 3-point range.[https://athletics.uindy.edu/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordan-loyd/6019 "Jordan Lloyd,"] athletics.uindy.edu. In 2015-16 Loyd finished his final Greyhound season averaging 20.9 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.9 assists, while shooting 50 percent from the field, 41 percent from 3-point range and 86 percent from the foul line. Loyd's name is all over the UIndy record book, as he finishes 25th all-time in scoring (1,213), fifth in career free throw percentage (.839), seventh in free throws made (329), 10th in 3-point percentage (.424), tied for 12th in 3-pointers made (132) and 16th in career scoring average (16.2). On March 2, 2016, Loyd earned a spot in the All-[[Great Lakes Valley Conference|GLVC]] First team and Defensive team.{{cite news|title=Loyd unanimous selection to All-GLVC First Team, also named to Defensive Team|url=http://athletics.uindy.edu/news/2016/3/2/mens-basketball-loyd-unanimous-selection-to-all-glvc-first-team-also-named-to-defensive-team.aspx|access-date=December 24, 2017|work=UIndy.edu|date=March 2, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2016–2017)=== Loyd went undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. On October 31, 2016, Loyd was selected with the 48th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA Development League Draft|2016 NBA D-League draft]] by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite news|title=Mad Ants Select Four Players, Perform Trade in 2016 NBA D-League Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/mad-ants-select-four-players-perform-trade-2016-nba-d-league-draft|access-date=December 24, 2017|work=nba.com|date=October 31, 2016}} In 49 games played during the 2016–17 season, Loyd averaged 15.1 points, 4.2 rebounds and 4 assists per game. ===Hapoel Eilat (2017–2018)=== On June 27, 2017, Loyd joined the [[Indiana Pacers]] and the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Pacers announce Summer League roster|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2017/06/27/pacers-announce-summer-league-roster/433260001/|access-date=December 24, 2017|work=indystar.com|date=June 27, 2017}}{{cite news|title=Raptors announce Summer League roster|url=http://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2017/06/27/raptors-announce-summer-league-roster-2/|access-date=December 24, 2017|work=raptorsrepublic.com|date=June 27, 2017}} On August 2, 2017, Loyd signed with the Israeli team [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=Jordan Loyd inks with Hapoel Eilat|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/243171/jordan-loyd-inks-with-hapoel-eilat.html|access-date=December 24, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=August 2, 2017}} On January 4, 2018, Loyd recorded a career-high 30 points, along with 11 rebounds and 2 assists in an 85–69 win over [[Ironi Nes Ziona]],{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 11: Nes Ziona Vs Hapoel Eilat|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23212&lang=en|access-date=January 4, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=January 4, 2018}} he was subsequently named [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 11 MVP]].{{cite news|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-11: ג'ורדן לויד|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17428|access-date=January 5, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=January 5, 2018|language=he}} On March 2, 2018, Loyd participated in the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#All-Star Game|Israeli League All-Star Game]] as a replacement for [[Derwin Kitchen]].{{cite news|title=אולסטאר: הזרים גברו על הישראלים|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17631|access-date=March 2, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=March 2, 2018|language=he}} Loyd led Eilat to the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Play-offs|2018 Israeli League Playoffs]], where they eventually lost to [[Hapoel Holon]]. Loyd finished the season as the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Points|league]] third-leading scorer with 17.4 points per game and also averaged 4.9 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals per game, with an .860 free three percentage (7th in the league). On June 8, 2018, Loyd earned a spot in the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#All-Israeli League Teams|All-Israeli League Second Team]].{{cite news|title=חמישיית העונה בליגת ווינר סל 2017/18|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19054|access-date=June 8, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=June 8, 2018|language=he}} ===Toronto Raptors (2018–2019)=== On June 25, 2018, Loyd signed a two-year deal with the Turkish team [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]].{{cite news|title=Darussafaka signs Jordan Loyd|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/278623/darussafaka-signs-jordan-loyd.html|access-date=June 25, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=June 25, 2018|archive-date=June 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625185903/https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/278623/darussafaka-signs-jordan-loyd.html|url-status=dead}} Four days later, Loyd joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] and the [[Boston Celtics]] for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Raptors announce Summer League roster|url=https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2018/06/29/raptors-announce-summer-league-roster-who-and-what-you-need-to-know/|access-date=June 29, 2018|work=raptorsrepublic.com|date=June 29, 2018}}{{cite news|title=Boston Celtics announce 2018 Summer League roster|url=https://www.celticsblog.com/2018/6/29/17519500/boston-celtics-announce-2018-summer-league-roster-nba-las-vegas-brad-stevens-danny-ainge-williams|access-date=June 29, 2018|work=celticsblog.com|date=June 29, 2018}} On August 7, 2018, after impressing during the Summer League, Loyd opted out of his deal with Darüşşafaka and signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite news|title=Raptors Sign Loyd To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-jordan-loyd-to-two-way-contract|access-date=August 7, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2018}} On October 29, 2018, he made his NBA debut playing two minutes in a 109–124 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news|title=Raptors at Bucks|url=https://watch.nba.com/game/20181029/TORMIL|access-date=October 30, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2018}} Loyd won a championship with the Raptors after they defeated the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2019 NBA Finals]]. Loyd became known as the "Random Guy in a Suit" due to being beside [[Kawhi Leonard]] during the famous Game 7 buzzer beater in the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], which he recognized by wearing a shirt with this slogan during the Raptors Championship parade.{{cite news|title='Random' Raptors player in viral Kawhi Leonard buzzer-beater photo had the best parade shirt|author=Andrew Joseph|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2019/06/jordan-loyd-raptors-player-random-suit-shirt-kawhi-leonard-buzzer-beater-parade-nba|access-date=April 19, 2020|work=USA Today|date=June 18, 2019}} Although Loyd did not play in the playoffs nor Finals, Loyd was credited as an important part of the Raptors' championship versus the Warriors, as Loyd was used as a fill-in for [[Stephen Curry]] during Raptors' practices, simulating Curry for defensive game planning.{{cite news|title=How the Raptors Solved Steph Curry|author=Kevin O'Connor|url=https://www.theringer.com/2019/6/8/18657848/toronto-raptors-steph-curry-defense|access-date=November 8, 2021|work=The Ringer|date=June 8, 2019}} On August 2, 2019, Loyd was waived by the Raptors.{{cite news|title=Raptors, Jordan Loyd part ways|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/raptors-jordan-loyd-part-ways/|access-date=August 2, 2019|work=Sportando.basketball|date=August 2, 2019|archive-date=August 3, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803142427/https://sportando.basketball/en/raptors-jordan-loyd-part-ways/|url-status=dead}} ===Valencia (2019–2020)=== On August 5, 2019, Loyd signed a one-year deal with [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite news |title=Valencia inks swingman Loyd |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9ukmicow8b47y9wr |access-date=August 5, 2019 |work=[[EuroLeague|EuroLeague.net]] |date=August 5, 2019}} On October 13, 2019, Loyd tied his career-high 30 points in his third league game with Valencia. He also recorded four rebounds, two assists and three steals in a 94–97 loss to [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]].{{cite news |title=Barça vs Valencia Basket - Jornada 4 - Liga Endesa |url=http://www.acb.com/partido/estadisticas/id/18665 |access-date=October 13, 2019 |work=ACB.com |date=October 13, 2019}} He averaged 12.0 points, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steal per game. ===Crvena Zvezda (2020–2021)=== On July 1, 2020, Loyd signed with [[KK Crvena Zvezda|Crvena Zvezda]].{{cite news |title=Jordan Loyd joins KK Crvena Zvedza |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jordan-loyd-joins-kk-crvena-zvedza/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 1, 2020 |date=July 1, 2020}} He was named Euroleague Round 2 MVP after scoring 30 points and adding 6 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 steals in a 90–73 win over [[Saski Baskonia]].{{cite web |title=Jordan Loyd named EuroLeague Round 2 MVP |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1112715/jordan-loyd-named-euroleague-round-2-mvp/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=October 12, 2020 |date=October 11, 2020}} For the season, he averaged 16.2 points, 3.1 assists, and 1.0 steals while shooting .888 from the free throw line.[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jordan-Loyd/Summary/31657 "Jordan Lloyd"], basketball.realgm.com. === Zenit Saint Petersburg (2021–2022) === On June 14, 2021, Loyd signed a two-year contract, though he only played with the team for one year, with Russian club [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. In 2021-22 he averaged 12.6 points, 4.2 rebounds, 4.4 assists, and 1.2 steals per game while shooting .849 from the free throw line. === AS Monaco (2022–2024) === On July 16, 2022, Loyd signed with [[AS Monaco Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] and the [[EuroLeague]], forming a formidable backcourt with [[Mike James (basketball, born 1990)|Mike James]] and [[Élie Okobo]].{{Cite web |title=Jordan Loyd, un renfort de poids pour la Roca Team |url=https://asmonaco.basketball/news/show.php?ID=38460 |access-date=2022-07-16 |website=asmonaco.basketball |language=fr-FR}} In 2022-23 he averaged 12.4 points, 2.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting .874 from the free throw line. In 2023–24 with the team he averaged 10.5 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 0.7 steals per game, while shooting .893 from the free throw line. === Maccabi Tel Aviv (2024) === On July 14, 2024, Loyd signed a two-year contract with Israeli powerhouse [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{cite web |title=Jordan Loyd officially joins Maccabi |url=https://basketnews.com/news-209157-jordan-loyd-officially-joins-maccabi.html |website=Basketnews.com |access-date=11 October 2024 |date=14 July 2024}} On October 10, Loyd mutually parted ways with the Israeli club due to the unstable political situation in the region.{{cite web |title=Jordan Loyd explains his departure: 'The uncertainty was too much' |url=https://basketnews.com/news-212750-jordan-loyd-explains-his-departure-the-uncertainty-was-too-much.html |website=Basketnews.com |access-date=11 October 2024 |date=10 October 2024}} === AS Monaco (2024–2025) === On October 12, 2024, Loyd returned to the [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] after leaving [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in Israel due to war concerns. He signed until 2026. Loyd would be immediately available for the team despite having already played twice in the Euroleague with another team.{{cite web |title=Jordan Loyd returns to Monaco with a contract until 2026 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1725765/jordan-loyd-monaco-maccabi-tel-aviv-euroleague-contract-2026/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=11 October 2024 |language=en |date=10 October 2024}}{{cite web |title=Jordan Loyd officially returns to AS Monaco |url=https://basketnews.com/news-212882-jordan-loyd-officially-returns-to-as-monaco.html |website=Basketnews.com |access-date=12 October 2024 |date=12 October 2024}} === Anadolu Efes (2025–present) === On September 20, 2025, Loyd signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/tr/news/nL8c7AHq8RGk5H2lkCaeYQ==|title=Jordan Loyd Anadolu Efes’te|last=|first=|date=September 20, 2025|website=|publisher=[[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]|language=En|access-date=September 20, 2025}} ==National team career== In August 2025, Loyd and fellow American-born player [[Jerrick Harding]] received Polish citizenship, and became eligible to play for the [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland national team]].{{Cite web |last=Media |first=Wirtualna Polska |title=Dobre wieści dla reprezentacji Polski. Prezydent złożył podpis |url=https://sportowefakty.wp.pl/koszykowka/1201931/dobre-wiesci-dla-reprezentacji-polski-prezydent-zlozyl-podpis |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=sportowefakty.wp.pl |language=pl}} In the game against [[Slovenia men's national basketball team|Slovenia]] at [[EuroBasket 2025]], he scored 32 points, thanks to which Poland defeated the rival 105–95. Loyd, together with [[Mateusz Ponitka]], led Poland to the quarterfinals, finished as the 5th top scorer of the tournament, and was selected to the [[FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Second Team]]. ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#AFE6BA; width:3em;"|† | Denotes seasons in which Loyd won the [[List of NBA champions|NBA Finals]] |} ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;background:#AFE6BA;"| {{nbay|2018}}† | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto]] | 12 || 0 || 4.6 || .444 || .500 || .818 || .7 || .5 || {{sort|-|—}} || {{sort|-|—}} || 2.4 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 12 || 0 || 4.6 || .444 || .500 || .818 || .7 || .5 || {{sort|-|—}} || {{sort|-|—}} || 2.4 {{S-end}} ===National team=== {{See also|Poland men's national basketball team}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:100%; text-align:right;" !
